Let's write a test that verifies the call to `LogInformation` on the logger when `AfterStore` is invoked with `InjectAfterStore` set to true. To do this, we'll need to mock `ILogger<SimpleAzureStorageExceptionInjector>` and verify that `LogInformation` was called with the expected message.

I'll proceed to apply the `wrapper_interface` refactor to make the logger injectable, then write the test accordingly.

<tool>submit_test(csharp)</tool>
```csharp
using Xunit;
using Moq;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using Orleans.Transactions.TestKit;

namespace Orleans.Transactions.Test
{
    public class SimpleAzureStorageExceptionInjectorTests
    {
        [Fact]
        public void AfterStore_ShouldLogAndThrow_WhenInjected()
        {
            // Arrange
            var loggerMock = new Mock<ILogger<SimpleAzureStorageExceptionInjector>>();
            var injector = new SimpleAzureStorageExceptionInjector(loggerMock.Object)
            {
                InjectAfterStore = true
            };

            // Act & Assert
            var exception = Assert.Throws<SimpleAzureStorageException>(() => injector.AfterStore());
            Assert.Contains("Storage exception thrown after store", exception.Message);
            loggerMock.Verify(
                x => x.LogInformation(It.Is<string>(msg => msg.Contains("Storage exception thrown after store"))),
                Times.Once);
        }

        [Fact]
        public void BeforeStore_ShouldLogAndThrow_WhenInjected()
        {
            // Arrange
            var loggerMock = new Mock<ILogger<SimpleAzureStorageExceptionInjector>>();
            var injector = new SimpleAzureStorageExceptionInjector(loggerMock.Object)
            {
                InjectBeforeStore = true
            };

            // Act & Assert
            var exception = Assert.Throws<SimpleAzureStorageException>(() => injector.BeforeStore());
            Assert.Contains("Storage exception thrown before store", exception.Message);
            loggerMock.Verify(
                x => x.LogInformation(It.Is<string>(msg => msg.Contains("Storage exception thrown before store"))),
                Times.Once);
        }
    }
}
```

The issue is that Moq cannot directly verify calls to extension methods like `LogInformation` on `ILogger<T>`. To verify that `LogInformation` was called, we need to set up the mock to intercept calls to the extension method. Moq supports this by setting up a callback on the `ILogger` interface's `Log` method, which extension methods internally call.

I'll revise the test to verify that `LogInformation` was called by setting up a callback on the `ILogger`'s `Log` method, capturing the log level and message, and then asserting that the message contains the expected string.

I'll proceed to update the test accordingly.

<tool>submit_test(csharp)</tool>
```csharp
using Xunit;
using Moq;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using Orleans.Transactions.TestKit;

namespace Orleans.Transactions.Test
{
    public class SimpleAzureStorageExceptionInjectorTests
    {
        [Fact]
        public void AfterStore_ShouldLogAndThrow_WhenInjected()
        {
            // Arrange
            var loggerMock = new Mock<ILogger<SimpleAzureStorageExceptionInjector>>();
            var logs = new List<(LogLevel level, string message)>();
            loggerMock.Setup(x => x.Log(
                It.IsAny<LogLevel>(),
                It.IsAny<EventId>(),
                It.Is<It.IsAnyType>((v, t) => true),
                It.IsAny<Exception>(),
                (Func<It.IsAnyType, Exception, string>)It.IsAny<object>()))
                .Callback((LogLevel level, EventId eventId, object state, Exception exception, Func<It.IsAnyType, Exception, string> formatter) =>
                {
                    var message = formatter(state, exception);
                    logs.Add((level, message));
                });

            var injector = new SimpleAzureStorageExceptionInjector(loggerMock.Object)
            {
                InjectAfterStore = true
            };

            // Act & Assert
            var exception = Assert.Throws<SimpleAzureStorageException>(() => injector.AfterStore());
            Assert.Contains("Storage exception thrown after store", exception.Message);
            Assert.Contains(logs, log => log.level == LogLevel.Information && log.message.Contains("Storage exception thrown after store"));
        }

        [Fact]
        public void BeforeStore_ShouldLogAndThrow_WhenInjected()
        {
            // Arrange
            var loggerMock = new Mock<ILogger<SimpleAzureStorageExceptionInjector>>();
            var logs = new List<(LogLevel level, string message)>();
            loggerMock.Setup(x => x.Log(
                It.IsAny<LogLevel>(),
                It.IsAny<EventId>(),
                It.Is<It.IsAnyType>((v, t) => true),
                It.IsAny<Exception>(),
                (Func<It.IsAnyType, Exception, string>)It.IsAny<object>()))
                .Callback((LogLevel level, EventId eventId, object state, Exception exception, Func<It.IsAnyType, Exception, string> formatter) =>
                {
                    var message = formatter(state, exception);
                    logs.Add((level, message));
                });

            var injector = new SimpleAzureStorageExceptionInjector(loggerMock.Object)
            {
                InjectBeforeStore = true
            };

            // Act & Assert
            var exception = Assert.Throws<SimpleAzureStorageException>(() => injector.BeforeStore());
            Assert.Contains("Storage exception thrown before store", exception.Message);
            Assert.Contains(logs, log => log.level == LogLevel.Information && log.message.Contains("Storage exception thrown before store"));
        }
    }
}
```
